75.title: Correct DFND solvent-volume precision and uncertainty claims
75.body:
## Source resolution — 2026-11-10

Resolved in [`b7b5a60`](https://github.com/uibcdf/topomt/commit/b7b5a60d8d46b84ca2a9f44bcb01eeac98a4b8b2), with qualification and current records published through `5a95efa`. Sampled endpoints now retain boundary-safe Clopper–Pearson intervals; bounded quadrature reports convergence/history or explicitly unknown error. Legacy fixed-order `exact` numeric values and tuple compatibility are preserved without an exactness claim.

The [archived resolution](https://github.com/uibcdf/topomt/blob/main/devguide/archive/dfnd_volume_precision_claims.md), [guard](https://github.com/uibcdf/topomt/blob/main/tests/test_dfnd_volume_precision_contract.py) and [matched three-case study](https://github.com/uibcdf/topomt/blob/main/docs/content/benchlab/synthetic/volume_measurements.md) retain the frozen protocol, analytic errors, 125/128 predeclared coverage result, independent integration and actual public receiving. Current card/hub/method/laboratory summaries are reconciled; original observations below remain history.

Scope: conditional numerical precision on declared finite supports in the source workspace. No universal deterministic quadrature bound, global accessible-volume/model/support/biological accuracy or installed/matrix claim. Wider references/support/paths stay #76/#60/#61 and installed qualification #16/#58. The final current-source notebook/site checkpoint remains under #76.

## Original report — retained history

## What

Make DFND numerical precision and uncertainty claims match the implemented volume methods. Fixed-order quadrature is exposed as `method='exact'` and returns no error estimate. Monte Carlo uses a normal-approximation `2 * sqrt(p*(1-p)/n)` half-width, which collapses to zero when every sample is empty or occupied. Some developer documentation calls that width rigorous and the quadrature volume exact.

## Evidence

Audited source: `7bd47faba6179a6e02444331e442acd251572564`, 2026-10-01. For the unit right tetrahedron and an interior sphere at `(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)`, radius 0.1, the analytic empty volume is `0.16247787646188028`. Quadrature returns:

| n_quad | volume |
|---:|---:|
| 6 | 0.16246969604365874 |
| 12 | 0.16247674509070278 |
| 24 | 0.16247772687537632 |
| 48 | 0.1624778572018284 |

The one-dimensional interval union is analytic, but the complete integral has discretization error. With radius 0.001, 8 Monte Carlo samples and seed 0, the same tetrahedron returns `(volume=1/6, error=0)`, although its true empty volume is strictly smaller. This is sampling uncertainty, not exact certainty. These cases were reproduced without changing runtime code.

## Acceptance

- Define the uncertainty contract and add tests for all-hit/no-hit and partial-hit sampling, including finite-sample coverage evidence.
- Choose a justified boundary-safe interval or explicitly bounded alternative; retain the difference between sampling uncertainty, numerical integration error and region/model error.
- Report deterministic quadrature method/order and convergence or error state honestly; retain an explicit compatibility/deprecation path for existing `exact` callers.
- Reconcile the metric documentation and maturity declarations; `canonical` semantic meaning does not certify zero numerical error or biological correctness.
- Scope this work to existing solvent-volume methods. Ligand occupancy is separately owned by #62 and must consume an honest precision contract.

Audit record: `devguide/archive/dfnd_volume_precision_claims.md` (created after this issue).
75.display_title: Correct DFND solvent-volume precision and uncertainty claims

151.title: Refine physical boundary connectivity beyond whole-face exterior clusters
151.body:
## Observed limitation

The fixed regular tetrahedron (edge 5.3 Å, atomic radii 1.7 Å) at probe 1.2 Å has four disconnected strict-clearance probe-center patches on its atomic-center convex-hull boundary. All six shared edges are blocked (expanded radius 2.9 Å exceeds half-edge 2.65 Å); each face has one free patch, independently verified under #150 by complete convex-intersection witnesses and four all-atom centroid rays.

The actual current public route yields one native external-link cluster, native family `percolating` with zero native wall faces, and one public `Percolating` with no promoted Mouth children. `_cluster_external_faces` joins whole admitted faces whenever they share an atomic edge, without checking whether free patches can cross that edge. The classifier applies its zero-wall-face override; the bridge preserves that contract. This is reproducible agreement with the discrete implementation, **not agreement of native link count with physical hull-patch count**. Existing prose calling the boundary fully solvent-permeable overstates what its face predicate establishes.

## Bounded follow-up and acceptance

1. Decide and document the relation among native face contacts, connected free boundary patches, public Mouth semantics and Percolating classification. Keep input/query/support identity separate from derived classification; do not simply rename this case Channel.
2. Start with a failing physical-connectivity regression on this frozen tetrahedron. Specify boundary-surface dependence, strictness/tolerances and all-atom exclusions. Reuse #150/#149 certificates as independent controls, including the opened shell one-patch case and closed-shell covered boundary. No new geometry or proteins is needed to start.
3. Implement the bounded chosen refinement with explicit support/provenance and distinguish unavailable refinement from computed zero. A shared atomic edge is insufficient evidence of a free connection; patch components on a face may also require refinement. Do not promote a triangle area as free aperture area or a local gate as a global bottleneck.
4. Exercise actual raw/public receiving, explicit units, source mapping, rigid motion, filtering and existing regressions. Correct affected scientific descriptions alongside behavior/contract changes. Preserve historical artifacts and explain compatibility.
5. Close with executed tests and a published decision/implementation; a tracking issue or prose correction alone does not deliver physical refinement.

#150 owns the independently certified reference and contrast only. #60 owns general public support/schema; #76 the broader independent panel; #75 volume precision. These remain separate. Current source qualification is source-workspace Python 3.14, not installed/matrix or biological validation.

180.title: Resolve bounded physical boundary receiving on the frozen straight tube
180.body:
## What

The new #178 straight-tube study has independently verified two physical hull patches at probe radii 1.2 and 1.4 Å, but original native/public receiving at source `b07a20e` returns `boundary_connectivity.status=unresolved`, `n_patches=None`, reason `face 17: arrangement work budget exhausted` for both controls (and at 2.5 Å).

## Scope and evidence

Input: `docs/content/benchlab/synthetic/straight_tube_narrow_dense/artifacts/straight_tube_narrow_dense_v1/input.json`, SHA-256 `2c389178d86bc2eb3cbbfd97e12aa14d70a71acb8759c1cb3061c2ef1a67a4b2`; 81 explicit argon balls, Å. Native protocol and `native_observations.json` retain full raw/public data. Separate `boundary_*A_v2_{certificate,verification,receipt}.json` independently prove 32 fully covered wall triangles and two free end patches across 14 end triangles; no free hull seams. Their checkers do not import DFND.

The native unresolved state is truthful and is not a computed zero. Earlier #151 source resolution concerned its five frozen controls, which remain historically resolved; it does not qualify this newly selected tube.

## Acceptance

Preserve original evidence. Start with the actual-public failing two-end targets in `tests/test_tube_study.py`; establish a generic, bounded algorithmic improvement with complete recoverable certificates and charged work, rather than increasing global budgets or special-casing a named input. Candidate direction: attempt positive convex-ball coverage of wall faces before expensive circle arrangements; retain unresolved outcomes where a proof is unavailable. Verify the same input/query, all earlier physical controls and resource use; review the DFND book and reconcile the comparative card/hub/lifecycle/case summaries before closure.

Owning local report will be `devguide/pending_proposals/dfnd_tube_boundary_budget.md`. This is a source boundary-decomposition limitation; no comparator inferiority, biological or installed-release claim.

Naming maintenance (#182, 2026-11-10): the current independently referenced input is `straight_tube_narrow_dense`; its wider catalog counterpart is `straight_tube_wide_sparse`. Current links use descriptive paths. Original scientific input/reference/native bytes and source scopes are unchanged; #180/#181 remain open. This changes no scientific finding state.

184.title: Resolve wide-tube physical boundary ordering within the numerical margin
184.body:
## What

The #183 wide/sparse tube has independently verified two physical hull openings at 2.5 Å, but actual native/public source `fdb253cf542e35d7d2b5414b7214677d0a884f24` returns `boundary_connectivity.status=unresolved`, `n_patches=None`, reason `face 12: critical-section ordering within numerical margin`. At 1.4 Å this same implementation resolves two physical patches. This is an availability limitation with a truthful unknown, not an incorrect computed patch count.

## Evidence and scope

77 full-precision argon balls, radii 1.88 Å, input SHA-256 `77fc6f703dac08084e75398202169c9f8e05fc07e75eec4faf400932a3f2a855`; with_connectors/flag_only/dryface, zero physical tolerances, epsilon/boundary margin 1e-6 Å. Evidence lives in `docs/content/benchlab/synthetic/straight_tube_wide_sparse/artifacts/straight_tube_wide_sparse_v1/`: frozen input/query, independently replayable wall/end/seam certificates and original native_observations.json. The independent 2.5 Å reference has 86 hull triangles, 68 completely covered wall triangles, 18 end triangles, four free end faces, two free seams and exactly two end patches. No production DFND routine supplies its oracle.

The actual-public target in `tests/test_wide_tube_study.py::test_wide_physical_boundary_matches_the_independent_reference` first fails at 2.5 Å. Preserve that result and the successful 1.4 Å control. #180 separately owns budget exhaustion (also observed at 5 Å on this wider input); #181 owns local/public versus all-atom exclusion.

## Acceptance

Diagnose the named face, recoverable events and declared numerical margins; implement any generic robust handling test-first with complete support/proof and bounded charged work. Do not weaken the strict physical reference or silently retune the query to claim this profile fixed. Verify both wide positive controls, the excluded control and adopted older cases; review the matching DFND book and reconcile card/hub/lifecycle/case/report before closure. No installed/platform or general biological claim.

Local report: `devguide/pending_proposals/wide_tube_boundary_numerics.md`.

195.title: Review POVME empty-initial-region failure before comparative reuse
195.body:
Observed during the maintainer-selected external POVME integration #193, with broader family/observable assessment #159. Provider/fork follow-up: https://github.com/uibcdf/POVME/issues/1 . This issue owns consumer evidence, source-specific applicability review and comparative-finding reconciliation, not a native implementation or an immediate scientific-kernel change.

A supplied inclusion sphere of radius 1 angstrom at [0,0,0], covered by an exclusion sphere of radius 4 angstrom at the same center (grid spacing 1 angstrom), leaves the initial ROI point field empty. The captured modern-source serial POVME worker raises a zero-size-array minimum reduction error before computing a frame volume; original frame handling filters the failed entry. The TopoMT adapter refuses to accept that as successful empty science, retains diagnostics and awards no completed-provider credit. A distinct evaluated-zero control, with points removed later by atom exclusion, works.

Exact observed profile: uibcdf/POVME@0c55f591dea3156e1ca76a486cf1f71d56c3a192, version 2.2.2+uibcdf.1; original scientific modules/serial methods unchanged from durrantlab/POVME@8a9f1973c25eb52e36e0d7b20183bf896cb66729; pymolecule@614a95a0b792f83fbee77e4c7eed7d5ce046dee1; Python 3.14.10, NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, Pydantic 2.14.3, Loguru 0.7.3, no Ray. Input: the synthetic 40-atom/two-chain PDB used by this integration. No coordinates were submitted remotely.

Keep the finding needs_review and exclude it from current scientific claims. The expected empty domain follows independently from inclusion being covered by exclusion; however no matched DFND operator/comparator study or upstream Python 3.12 run is claimed. This is an execution/empty-input contract observation, not demonstrated geometric inferiority or a DFND advantage.

Retain tests/data/original_local/povme/povme-failed.zip, the corresponding configuration/diagnostics and tests/test_specialist_original_execution.py::test_original_specialist_failures_never_become_empty_success. Review the original intended input domain and any proposed provider correction in its own issue. Before resolving this finding, require the same-source/query correction or explicit retained-domain decision, meaningful regression evidence and synchronized card/hub/register/method summary/issue history. A newer version or closure of #193 alone is not a correction.

Detailed local record: devguide/pending_bugs/povme_empty_initial_roi.md. Broader installed/public support remains #101/#16. The selected compatibility fork preserves scientific code in this delivery; an external upstream issue/PR still requires separate maintainer publication authorization.

Canonical maintained finding card: [povme-empty-initial-region](https://github.com/uibcdf/topomt/discussions/154#discussioncomment-19552378), lifecycle `needs_review`, linked from the hub review queue and the POVME resource thread. The card, register, failed bundle and this open issue retain the same bounded observed scope.
